cards.text: This is a psalm David wrote for the choirmaster, and friend, he SKIPS the small talk. No 'hello,' no 'how's Your week.' The first words out of his mouth to the LORD are: "How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever?"

cards.question: David asks the LORD, "Will You forget me forever?" What does that question tell you about how David feels?

answers.text: He feels he forgot about God
He feels sure God is near

cards.text: He keeps going. He asks how long the LORD will hide His face, and how long he has to wrestle in his soul with sorrow in his heart each day. EACH DAY. That's not one rough Monday, friend. That's a rough WHOLE CALENDAR.

cards.question: God feels far away, but David has trouble down here too. He asks how long someone will dominate him. Who is it?

cards.text: Count them up. David asks "How long" FOUR times in two verses. That's a man pressing the elevator button over and over, like the doors are gonna feel bad about it.

cards.question: Every one of David's "how long" questions is about God hiding His face.

cards.text: Then the questions stop, and David asks for something instead: "Consider me and respond, O LORD my God." And he wants God to give light to his eyes.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to give light to his eyes. What does David say could happen if that light doesn't come?

cards.text: And it's not only his life on the line. David's thinking about who'd be watching if he went down. Same as all of us. You trip in public, and the FIRST thing you check is who saw.

cards.question: David says that if he falls, his foes will mourn for him.

cards.text: Then David drops one little word. Real quiet. ... But.

cards.question: After all those "how long" questions, what does David say he has trusted in?
David's foes would rejoice if he fell. Now David says his ___ will rejoice in the LORD's salvation.

cards.text: And David wraps up the whole psalm with a song for the LORD. Five verses ago this man was asking if God forgot him, and now he's WARMING UP HIS VOICE!

cards.question: David says he will sing to the LORD. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD has been good to him
His enemy has finally run off
The choirmaster asked for a song

findings.problem: Card 5 tells nothing new. It recounts the 'how long' questions from verses 1-2, which cards 1 and 3 already told, so it is a recap card and does not move the passage forward. Its joke could ride on card 3 instead.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'His king' can be argued as right. Saul, Israel's king, pursued David as an enemy (1 Samuel 18-26). A baker who knows David's life could say the enemy is his king. The psalm never names the enemy.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The answers do not sound alike. 'The LORD's loving devotion' uses distinctive Bible wording. 'His years of experience' sounds modern. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question's own setup line, 'David's foes would rejoice if he fell,' rules out the wrong answer 'foes'. A sentence saying his foes will rejoice in the LORD's salvation makes no sense right after that setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The enemy's boast in verse 4, 'I have overcome him,' is never told on any card. Card 9 only says David is thinking about who'd be watching. Card 10 covers only the foes rejoicing. The baker misses a key line of verse 4.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card uses Psalm 13:1 ('Five verses ago this man was asking if God forgot him') but cites only Psalm 13:6.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. It is used on 5 of the 8 choice cards (2, 4, 8, 12, 15). True or false is used on 2 and fill in the blank on 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
